title: Capacitor geometries requiring quantitative analysis
body: The only capacitor geometries AP Physics C: E&M expects students to analyze and describe quantitatively.

items.label: Parallel-plate capacitor
items.meaning: Two separated parallel conducting plates holding equal and opposite charge.

items.label: Concentric spherical capacitor
items.meaning: Two concentric spherical conducting surfaces holding equal and opposite charge.

items.label: Coaxial cylindrical capacitor
items.meaning: Two coaxial cylindrical conducting surfaces holding equal and opposite charge.

caution: Do not use the parallel-plate formula C = \kappa\varepsilon_0 A/d for the spherical or cylindrical geometries. Derive C = Q/\Delta V from that geometry's own Q and \Delta V expressions.
ced_evidence: 10.3 Boundary Statement: "only expects the quantitative analysis and description of parallel-plate capacitors, concentric spherical capacitors, and coaxial cylindrical capacitors"

title: Field between parallel plates
caution: This holds only when the plate separation is much smaller than the plate dimensions, and away from the edges. It comes from Gauss's law plus superposition. The field is proportional to the surface charge density on either plate.
ced_evidence: 10.3.A.3.i "magnitude of the electric field between two charged parallel plates... determined by applying Gauss's law and the principle of superposition"; 10.3.A.3.ii

title: Dielectric constant
caution: The E_0/E form applies to an isolated capacitor, whose charge stays fixed when the dielectric is inserted. With the dielectric, the field is reduced and the capacitance increases (C = \kappa C_0).
ced_evidence: 10.4.A.2 "dielectric constant of a material relates the electric permittivity of that material to the permittivity of free space"; 10.4.A.4; 10.4.A.5
